question.:question/problem:
Find where the normal line to the curve $y=-4\sqrt{x}+3x+2$ at the point with $x$-coordinate $1$ intersects the $x$-axis.

The intersection is $(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$. Give exact values.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First find the point on the curve.

$$
f(1)=-4\sqrt{(1)}+3(1)+2=1.
$$

The normal passes through $(1,1)$.

Rewrite the radical or reciprocal using powers, then differentiate.

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=- 4 x^{\frac{1}{2}} + 3 x + 2, \\f'(x)&=3 - \frac{2}{x^{\frac{1}{2}}}=3 - \frac{2}{\sqrt{x}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope and take its negative reciprocal to find the normal slope.

$$
\begin{aligned}
m_t=f'(1)&=3 - \frac{2}{\sqrt{(1)}}=1, \\m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}&=-\frac{1}{(1)}=-1.
\end{aligned}
$$

Use point-slope form through $(1,1)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-(1)&=-1(x-(1)), \\y&=- x + 2.
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=-1x+(2), \\x&=2.
\end{aligned}
$$

The intersection is $(2,0)$.

f(x)&=- 4 x^{\frac{1}{2}} - 2 x, \\f'(x)&=-2 - \frac{2}{x^{\frac{1}{2}}}=-2 - \frac{2}{\sqrt{x}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope and take its negative reciprocal to find the normal slope.

$$
\begin{aligned}
m_t=f'(1)&=-2 - \frac{2}{\sqrt{(1)}}=-4, \\m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}&=-\frac{1}{(-4)}=\frac{1}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Use point-slope form through $(1,-6)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-(-6)&=\frac{1}{4}(x-(1)), \\y&=\frac{x}{4} - \frac{25}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $y$-axis, $x=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&=\frac{1}{4}\cdot 0+\left(- \frac{25}{4}\right), \\y&=- \frac{25}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The intersection is $(0,- \frac{25}{4})$.
